venue.name: Miniature World
venue.description: Miniature World is a paid indoor attraction inside the Fairmont Empress Hotel at 649 Humboldt Street in downtown Victoria. It holds over 85 miniature dioramas and displays, including one of the world's largest model railways, two large dollhouses, a circus, castles and a working sawmill, with lighting, sound and animation. It is open every day from 10:00 to 21:00, with the last admission sold at 20:15. Groups of five or more paying guests take a small amount off each admission, and it has been a destination for class trips for years.
venue.address: 649 Humboldt St., Victoria, BC, Canada V8W 1A7

facility_notes.bus_parking: As we are located on a busy street with little to no parking, we recommend leaving your vehicle at one of the multiple downtown parkades for your convenience. The nearest parkades are located at 743 View street and at 575 Yates street, both a five minute walk from our location.

venue.hours_notes: Open 7 days a week, Monday to Sunday 10:00 to 21:00, with the last admission sold at 20:15. Hours may vary on long weekends and statutory holidays, and it may be temporarily closed for private viewings or events. They ask visitors to arrive at least 45 minutes before closing.

programs.name: Group and Class Field Trip
programs.description: A self guided walk through the dioramas at a group rate. The published admission is $22.50 for adults, $15.25 for youth 13 to 17, $11.25 for children 5 to 12 and free for tots 0 to 4. Groups of 5 to 9 paying guests take $1.00 off each admission and groups of 10 or more take $1.50 off each, so in a group of ten a child aged 5 to 12 pays $9.75 and an adult pays $21.00. All admissions are subject to 5% tax. Book through the online booking page or phone them.
programs.what_children_do: Walk from one lit glass case to the next at their own pace, looking at model trains crossing trestle bridges, dollhouses, castles, a circus ground and a spaceship, with sound and moving parts to watch.
programs.our_note: It is all behind glass, so this is a looking visit and not a touching one. It sits inside the Empress on a busy street with almost no parking, so plan how you will drop off and pick up. The site never says how long a class should allow or how many adults have to come, so ask when you phone.
programs.practical_summary: Fully indoors, open every day, and a little cheaper per person once you have five in the group. Washrooms, a lunch spot, step free access and bus parking are not mentioned anywhere on the site, so it is worth a call.
programs.extra_fees_note: All admissions are subject to 5% tax.
programs.evidence: Large Groups of 10+ paying guests receive $1.50 each off regular admission.

images.alt: A large model landscape of green hills and a blue river dotted with small white castles, with a model train crossing a bridge in the foreground.
A model steam locomotive pulling red carriages across a tall wooden trestle bridge in a miniature mountain landscape, with the words Canadian Pacific Railway across the top.
A miniature circus ground packed with big top tents, a ferris wheel and fairground rides, with the words Circus World across the top.
A model Tudor style house with lit windows, brick chimneys and tiny figures at the door, with the word Dollhouses across the top.
